## Match: 86% – strong fit

Calculation: must 0.80 × 0.7 + nice 1.00 × 0.3
The core stack of the JD maps almost 1:1 to the CV: 7+ years of Swift/iOS, architecture patterns, REST, APNs, CI/CD with Bitrise, XCTest. Partial zones: GraphQL (not in the CV), XCUITest (unit testing is strong, UI testing is not documented), security/privacy as a formal discipline (the access-management domain is close but not the same). The decisive unknown is not technical at all: Team Anywhere requires an Atlassian legal entity in the employee's country – Belarus is unconfirmed. Main action: resolve location eligibility before investing interview time.

## Verdict

Technically a strong fit for a Senior role at scale. The employer's pain is security, reliability and audit at massive scale – this is exactly where the 99.8% crash-free / 500K+ DAU story plays. Risks in order: (1) Belarus eligibility under Team Anywhere, (2) GraphQL + XCUITest gaps, (3) compensation not published. Recommend applying only after a recruiter answer on location; the drafts are prepared accordingly.

## Gap 1: GraphQL APIs (partial in requirements)

There is no GraphQL in the work history, so this gap cannot be closed with real experience and must not be faked. What transfers is API-contract work at scale: the client-side synchronization between mobile apps, user accounts and distributed backends was designed around explicit REST contracts, versioning and error semantics – the same design muscle GraphQL schemas demand. For the interview, be upfront: strong REST design experience, GraphQL fundamentals learned on the side.

- Designed client-side synchronization between mobile apps, user accounts and distributed REST/JSON backends, including contract versioning and error handling (Property & Access Management Platform, 500K+ DAU).
- Compensation: learn GraphQL client fundamentals (queries, mutations, caching) before a technical round; describe REST-to-GraphQL as a transferable API-design skill, not as hands-on experience.

## Gap 2: XCUITest / UI testing (partial in requirements)

Unit testing is strong and documented; UI test automation is not. The honest close is the testing culture itself: taking coverage from 13% to 75% with XCTest and Swift Testing, wiring checks into CI, and using ViewInspector for view-level assertions – the same discipline XCUITest extends to the UI layer.

- Increased unit test coverage from 13% to 75% and wired tests and static checks into the CI pipeline (XCTest, Swift Testing, ViewInspector; Azure DevOps, Bitrise, GitHub Actions).
- Compensation: review XCUITest basics (synchronization, page objects, CI integration) before interviews and frame the testing philosophy: catch regressions before release at the cheapest possible layer.

## Gap 3: Security and privacy discipline (partial in requirements)

The JD is about Guard – security and data governance – and asks for a security-conscious mindset when handling sensitive data. Direct secure-SDLC documentation is thin in the CV, but the domain is close: access management flows with permissions, restrictions and error handling on products with sensitive user data, plus a private-by-design personal product. The close is to make this domain experience visible rather than to claim security certifications.

- Developed access-management flows with permissions, restrictions and error handling for a platform serving 160K+ DAU, working with sensitive user data and account states (Swift, UIKit, Combine).
- Designed a private-by-design personal product (Between: Decision Journal): user reflections stay in a private journal with user-controlled data lifecycle (SwiftUI, Swift backend).
- Compensation: prepare concrete mobile security practices to speak about (Keychain storage, certificate pinning, data minimization, jailbreak/root detection) as working knowledge.

## What cannot be closed (honestly)

- **Hands-on GraphQL** → compensation: transferable REST API design + fast self-study; state it openly in interviews.
- **XCUITest hands-on** → compensation: XCUITest basics before interviews; strong unit-testing culture as the foundation.
- **Formal security/privacy engineering** → compensation: domain adjacency (access management) + prepared talking points on mobile security practices.
- **Location eligibility (Belarus under Team Anywhere)** → not a CV gap but the hard gate: resolve with the recruiter before any interview investment.

cover_letter:
Guard is the part of Atlassian I find most concrete: the security and data-governance layer where admins get centralized controls and visibility, and where leaders can safely push AI adoption. The mobile side of that mission – letting customers monitor activity, investigate issues and stay in control from anywhere – is exactly the product surface I want to work on: security functionality that has to feel instant and trustworthy on a phone.

My background is 7+ years of native iOS with Swift: architecture patterns, REST APIs, APNs, CI/CD and XCTest. In my current project I own business-critical flows for a platform serving 160K+ DAU and contribute to a 99.8% crash-free rate; earlier I shipped permission and guest-access flows for an application serving 500K+ DAU. I also raised unit test coverage from 13% to 75% to keep regressions out of releases. The transferable skill for Guard is handling sensitive data in access-management products: permissions, restrictions and error states that users must trust.

The challenge I see: audit and security UX is dense, and on mobile it must stay fast while feature parity with web is kept across teams. One idea is to make reliability part of the security experience itself: a performance budget and crash-free goals for the mobile audit flows, backed by validated event tracking so investigations run on trustworthy data. I would be glad to discuss how I could help with that.

## TL;DR

Atlassian – large product company behind Jira, Confluence, Trello, Loom and other teamwork tools; the open role is in Audit Platform and Guard, the security and data-governance layer, bringing security and audit experiences to native iOS. Technical match is high and the reliability/security focus fits the profile. The one hard unknown: Team Anywhere requires a country where Atlassian has a legal entity – Belarus availability is unconfirmed and must be answered before investing interview time.

## Product and market

- Products named on the careers site: Rovo, Jira, Jira Align, Jira Service Management, Confluence, Loom (job page footer, 2026-10-20).
- The Guard/Audit Platform team: "the security and data-governance layer for Atlassian" – centralized controls and visibility for admins, protecting sensitive data, governance and risk management at scale; the mobile mission is to let customers "monitor activity, investigate issues, and stay in control wherever they are" (job posting).
- Market position, revenue, competitors: no data verified in this research (public company facts not checked this session).

## Technology and stack

- From the JD: Swift, native iOS, test-driven development (XCTest, XCUITest), REST/GraphQL APIs, APNs, CI/CD with Fastlane and Bitrise, performance work (launch time, memory, network), crash monitoring, some frontend web stack work.
- Android experience is "a plus but not required" – cross-platform awareness valued.
- Engineering culture: the Atlassian Engineering handbook describes autonomous teams built on "ownership, trust, and a common language" ([atlassian.com/blog/how-we-build/handbook](https://www.atlassian.com/blog/how-we-build/handbook)).
- Specific iOS architecture, library choices, blog posts by the mobile team: no data found.

## Team and culture

- Team Anywhere (since 2020): employees choose office, home, or a mix; work is possible from any country where Atlassian has a legal entity, with sufficient timezone overlap with the team, team lead approval and legal right to work in the region ([globalcareers-atlassian.icims.com quote](https://globalcareers-atlassian.icims.com/company/careers/teamanywhere), [kadence.co, 03.04.2025](https://kadence.co/news/why-atlassian-is-sticking-with-distributed-work/)).
- Reported scale: ~12,000 employees (kadence.co, 03.04.2025).
- Benefits reported by aggregators: 26 weeks paid leave for birthing parents, 20 weeks for non-birthing parents (4dayweek.io – aggregator data, treat as secondary).
- Team '27 conference announced in San Francisco (events.atlassian.com/team).
- Glassdoor/DOU reviews, mobile team size: no data collected.

## Hiring process

- Application via the careers site ("Apply for this job", iCIMS-backed flow).
- Interview stages, recruiter responsiveness: no data in this research.

## Flags

🟢 High technical match: Swift/iOS core requirements map almost 1:1 to the profile (7+ years, architecture patterns, REST, APNs, CI/CD incl. Bitrise, XCTest).
🟢 Security, reliability and sensitive-data focus matches the reliability track record (99.8% crash-free on 160K+ DAU; access-management domain).
🟢 Team Anywhere and distributed, cross-functional collaboration fit the target format (remote work from Belarus).
🔴 Team Anywhere country rule: needs an Atlassian legal entity in the employee's country. Belarus is unconfirmed and likely unsupported – this is a stop-or-go question before spending interview time. Contract/EOR alternatives: unknown.
🔴 Compensation not published in the JD; the profile floor is 4500 USD gross/month – likely fine for Atlassian, but the actual range for this location must be confirmed.
🟡 GraphQL and XCUITest appear in requirements but are not in the CV (partial gaps).

## Questions to ask them

- Is Team Anywhere available for candidates based in Belarus (legal entity, contractor/EOR, or not at all)? If not, is any alternative arrangement possible?
- What is the timezone overlap expectation for this team and where is the team distributed?
- What is the compensation range for this role from Belarus?
- How is the iOS stack evolving in Guard (SwiftUI adoption, architecture patterns, GraphQL usage)?
- How is UI testing (XCUITest) organized: what coverage do they expect from a senior engineer?
- What does the interview process look like and what does the security-domain onboarding include?
